page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the n4-standard-32 demonstrates strong performance in memory-intensive and multi-threaded operations. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks place the instance in the top 25% of tested systems, achieving 211.52 GB/sec for read-only operations and 99.63 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 16013.0 and high throughput in static web serving at 44.06 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 296.22 tokens/sec on small 135M LLM models, though performance drops to a poor 2.31 tokens/sec for large 70B models. Single-core CPU performance, cryptography, and database operations consistently fall within the average range.

The n4-standard-32 offers balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring a steady ratio of compute to memory without the overhead of dedicated local storage or GPU hardware. The presence of hardware-accelerated instructions like AMX and AVX-512 allows the instance to handle lightweight machine learning inference and vector calculations efficiently on the CPU. This instance is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, image processing, and medium-scale database operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-32 is a general-purpose server configured with 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs from Intel, 16 physical cores, and 128 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPUs, it relies on network-attached resources. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. In benchmarks, the instance shows strong multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 16013.0, and high-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 211.52 GB/sec for large-block reads. It also delivers strong static web serving throughput of 44.06 GB/sec and efficient text generation for small LLM models. However, performance drops significantly for large 70B LLM models. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads, making it suitable for multi-threaded applications, image processing, software compilation, and general-purpose web serving.
